title: Construction Managers and Quantity Surveyors

claims.text: Safe Work Australia published guidance (23 July 2026) that AI and digital technologies are a work health and safety matter requiring the normal WHS risk-management process, and NSW's WHS Amendment (Digital Work Systems) Act 2026 is the first law imposing express WHS duties on employers using AI, automation and digital platforms - binding construction managers who introduce site cameras, scheduling tools or AI assistants.

sources.publisher: The Good Builder (reporting Safe Work Australia guidance and NSW WHS Amendment Act 2026)
sources.title: AI Workplace Safety Guidance: What Builders Should Know
sources.whatItMeasured: Reports Safe Work Australia's July 2026 AI/digital-tech WHS guidance and the NSW Digital Work Systems Act 2026
sources.quote: Safe Work Australia has just made clear that those changes carry a safety obligation. The national policy body has released guidance explaining the work health and safety implications of introducing or changing AI and digital technologies at work.

sources.title: Australian WHS Legislative Updates
sources.whatItMeasured: Records Safe Work Australia's new AI and Digital Technologies WHS guidance (published 23 July 2026)
sources.quote: Safe Work Australia has released new guidance on managing work health and safety risks associated with artificial intelligence and digital technologies.

claims.scope: National model WHS plus NSW (first jurisdiction with express digital-work-systems duties); primary duties in NSW not yet all commenced as at mid-2026. Binds PCBUs, including construction managers.
claims.refuteNotes: Two independent trade/regulatory summaries of the same Safe Work Australia guidance and NSW Act; population and window match. 2 of 3 skeptics failed to overturn.

claims.text: State builder licensing (NSW Fair Trading, Victorian Building Authority, QBCC) holds the licensed builder responsible for the accuracy of representations and quote claims, including AI-generated content - so a construction manager cannot delegate accuracy to a generative tool.

sources.publisher: Mindiam (AI for Trades and Construction in Australia)
sources.title: AI for Trades and Construction in Australia
sources.whatItMeasured: States the regulatory frame that state builder licensing holds the licensed builder responsible for AI-generated representations
sources.quote: State builder licensing (NSW Fair Trading, Victorian Building Authority, QBCC) holds the licensed builder responsible for accuracy of representations and quote claims - including AI-generated content.

claims.scope: State-licensed building work in NSW/VIC/QLD; the PCBU/supervisor must review and adopt AI output rather than rely on it.
claims.refuteNotes: Real industry summary of state licensing obligations; population and window match. 2 of 3 skeptics failed to overturn.

claims.text: O*NET lists Construction Managers' tasks as inspecting projects for building and safety-code compliance, preparing budgets and progress reports, negotiating contracts, and directing drone use for site inspections and progress monitoring - and reports US employment of 550,300 with projected growth of 7% or higher (2024-2034), much faster than average.

sources.publisher: O*NET OnLine (US Department of Labor) / BLS
sources.title: 11-9021.00 - Construction Managers
sources.whatItMeasured: Occupational task taxonomy and US BLS employment/growth projections for Construction Managers
sources.quote: Direct how drone technology is used for site inspections and progress monitoring, ensuring accurate and timely project completion. Employment (2024) 550,300 employees. Projected growth (2024-2034) Much faster than average (7% or higher).

claims.scope: US O*NET/BLS data; task composition is indicative, and the employment/growth figures are US, not Australian.
claims.refuteNotes: Primary occupational database; US population and employment counts explicitly scoped; in-window. 2 of 3 skeptics failed to overturn.

claims.text: AGC of America's 2026 outlook reports 61% of contractors use AI or plan to increase AI investment, with office/administrative tasks (45%) and estimating (23%) the most-adopted functions; a 2026 MDPI systematic review of 191 articles (2020-2025) found AI adoption in construction remains fragmented and inconsistent across organisations and regions.

sources.title: AI Agents for Construction: Statistics & Trends
sources.whatItMeasured: Reports AGC 2026 outlook on contractor AI use and function-level adoption
sources.quote: AGC's 2026 outlook reported 61% use AI or plan to increase AI investment... Office or administrative tasks: 45% Estimating: 23%.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) in Construction Management (CM): A Systematic Review of Models and Methods
sources.whatItMeasured: Systematic review of 191 peer-reviewed articles (2020-2025) on AI in construction management
sources.quote: their adoption in CM remains fragmented and inconsistent across organizations and regions

claims.scope: Predominantly US/global contractor surveys and literature; Australian adoption is implied, not measured. MDPI direct fetch returned 403 (abstract retrieved via search index; page renders in browser).
claims.refuteNotes: Named industry survey (AGC) plus peer-reviewed review; global population noted in scope; MDPI 403 is a bot block, not a dead link. 2 of 3 skeptics failed to overturn.
